blocks.text: Polymers are very large molecules made by joining many small molecules, called monomers, through polymerisation. Organic polymers are modern materials of great importance: their properties and low cost have made life easier and more efficient. Polymers are found everywhere, from shopping bags (poly(ethene)) and clothesline (poly(propene)) to bulletproof vests (Kevlar) and aerospace materials.

The properties of polymers vary with the type and number of monomers and the way they are made. Some, such as poly(ethene) and poly(propene), are light and soft and suit uses that need soft materials. Others, such as Kevlar, are hard and thermally very stable and are used as hard, durable materials, for example in bulletproof vests.

blocks.title: Keep in mind: systematic names of polymers
blocks.text: Synthetic polymers are named by writing 'poly' before the name of the monomer: polythene is poly(ethene) and polyvinyl chloride is poly(chloroethene). For polymers made from two or more monomers common names are usually used, because the systematic name is too long: poly(ethane-1,2-diyl benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate) is called polyethylene terephthalate, PET (PETE).
